bib.title: CCNet: Extracting High Quality Monolingual Datasets from Web Crawl Data
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v2; LREC 2020 not printed in PDF)

read.skipped: Table 3 per-language rows skimmed (en, gu, ur checked)

question: How can high-quality monolingual corpora in many languages be extracted from Common Crawl automatically?
hypothesis: Deduplicating before language ID and bucketing documents by perplexity under a Wikipedia language model yields better pretraining data than unfiltered Common Crawl or Wikipedia.
contributions: Open pipeline (dedup, fastText LID, KenLM perplexity bucketing) that preserves document structure
Wikipedia SentencePiece and 5-gram KenLM models for 48 languages
Dataset statistics for the Feb 2019 snapshot (174 languages)
Tool to reproduce the dataset from a URL list

method.summary: Per Common Crawl WET snapshot: shard into 5GB JSON, deduplicate normalised paragraphs by 64-bit SHA-1 hash, fastText language ID (keep score above 0.5), then score documents by KenLM perplexity under a per-language Wikipedia model and split each language into head/middle/tail thirds. Nothing is removed on LM score. Quality is checked by training fastText vectors and BERT-Base on the buckets.

datasets.size: 24TB uncompressed text, about 3B pages, 1600 shards of 5GB; output 3.2TB compressed, 174 languages, 1.5B documents

datasets.name: Wikipedia (LM training and BERT baseline)
datasets.size: English LM trained on 534M text, Gujarati 12M; BERT baselines 16G en, 5G ru, 1.1G zh, 106M ur

datasets.name: XNLI

limits: No variance or seeds; one run per Table 2 cell.
Wikipedia comparison confounds quality with quantity: CC head has more data for ru, zh, ur.
Head vs middle vs tail was tested on fastText only; BERT used head only, so no BERT evidence on the tail.
Perplexity under a Wikipedia LM penalises valid text with different vocabulary (blog comments, jargon forums), conceded by the authors.
LM size varies by language (English 534M vs Gujarati 12M), so thresholds are set per language.
BERT hyperparameters (lr, batch size, steps) not given.
